svg.text: hole: grown-up pokes with a pencil/awl
Calibration: the black bar must measure
exactly 100 mm and the square 20x20 mm.
Use card ~1 mm (cereal box) for parts.
github.com/dev-repos/kids-robotics-projects · Kids.JoinDev · CC BY 4.0 · Grown-ups do all craft-knife cutting.
Glue a 22 mm hip peg in
The motor turns both cranks, half a turn apart.
The crank pin (with a straw roller) slides up and
down in the leg slot and pushes the leg front
and back. The leg swings like a pendulum from
the hip peg: the foot (red) sweeps 56 mm along
the table and rises only 4 mm. One foot pushes back
while the other swings forward - and his hands
push the barrow! Roller never leaves the slot.
• A grown-up uses the hot glue gun,
craft knife, and pokes the holes.
• Snip the sharp skewer tips off.
• Fingers away from the cranks when ON.
• Batteries the right way round; never
join the wires; take them out after.
• Keep small parts from little kids.
